forcedChoices.choice: tú for the lawyer speaking to Jesus
forcedChoices.reason: Packet rule: a person speaking to one person uses tú; the same for the lepers, Simon, the Pharisee at Gerasa, and Thomas.

forcedChoices.choice: » at the start of each continued paragraph of a quote
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish convention for a quote that runs across paragraphs; the English opens each paragraph with a quote mark.
The English writes 'straight' (not 'strait'); 'recto' keeps the English word, 'estrecho' carries 'narrow'.

forcedChoices.choice: ustedes (plural) in Jesus' answer to Thomas
forcedChoices.reason: 'Do we not all live' and the group setting show that Jesus speaks to all the apostles.
'realm' kept as 'reino' to match earlier papers ('child of the realm'); the context is the world, not the kingdom of heaven.
Spanish dates use no ordinal suffix, so the sup tag stays empty; Spanish puts the era after the year, so the scaps span moved after 74.
The English continues the sentence after the question mark with lowercase 'if'; Spanish allows lowercase after ? to keep one sentence.
